overall_assessment: Anonymization generally works well across all 28 packet records: no personal-data leaks, residual administrative dates, or removal-induced text/structure damage were observed in the supplied text. All five suspect flags are false alarms: four removal-share flags reflect correct semester-year removal from very short records, and the name_like flag concerns the course title Core concepts in Digital Investigation & Forensics. One random control loses a substantive publication date for official guidelines; every other displayed removed span is an appropriate administrative semester-year removal.

findings.evidence: … avhør av sårbare mistenkte. Riksadvokaten utga [−høsten 2023−] retningslinjer for politiavhør av barn og …
findings.description: The publication date of Riksadvokaten’s guidelines for interviewing children and particularly vulnerable suspects is removed. This dates an official subject-matter document, rather than course administration or a teaching semester, and must be preserved under the content-year and government-document rules. This unflagged problem occurs in one of the 23 random controls.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: In R/anonymize.R, .anon_generic() removes inflected season-plus-year expressions using .season_regex. Its .not_gov guard recognizes document/publisher cues only within the preceding 80 characters; .gov_doc_regex does not include Riksadvokaten, and the document cue retningslinjer follows the date in this sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the government-document guard to recognize Riksadvokaten as an official publisher and preserve season-year publication dates in bounded same-line patterns such as Riksadvokaten utga <season year> retningslinjer. Add a regression case preserving this sentence while still removing the course-header (Høst 2024).
